headline: High: Mentat’s broad filesystem/network defaults can conflict with Botpress’s agentic outputs, creating unsafe shared-workspace and downstream-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is an agentic chatbot that can emit instruction-like content, while Mentat reads files and uses stdin/stdout with filesystem-based shared state. That creates a plausible prompt-injection bridge if Botpress output is copied into files or terminal input. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Botpress output is copied into files or terminal input that Mentat later parses as instructions
IF both agents operate in the same workspace without content provenance checks
mitigations: Keep Botpress and Mentat in separate workspaces
Require manual review before Mentat consumes Botpress-generated text
Strip instructions from Botpress outputs before reuse
Use a provenance tag or prefix for machine-generated content
requires-engineering: add content-isolation and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat reads and writes filesystem content and sends data to a configured model provider, while Botpress is a customer-support agent with no explicit egress listed. If they share a workspace, source code or other files touched by Mentat can flow into Botpress prompts or logs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Botpress and Mentat share a workspace or logs containing source code
IF Mentat forwards file contents to its model provider during normal operation
mitigations: Separate customer-support and coding workspaces
Avoid placing secrets or sensitive files in the shared directory
Disable or redact file-content logging where possible
Review what Mentat sends to the model provider
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model explicitly shares state via filesystem. Botpress has package-install capability and is an agentic system that may also act on shared artifacts. If both touch the same repo or directory, concurrent writes and git-state races can cause destructive conflicts; the shared-write pathway is directly supported by Mentat’s profile, while Botpress’s write surface is not documented, so uncertainty still favors high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem path or git repository
IF Botpress performs any file or package changes in that shared location
mitigations: Run the agents in separate repositories
Serialize access to any shared git working tree
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Require lockfiles or a coordinator before edits
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Botpress can generate agentic outputs, and Mentat is a coding assistant that applies diff-based edit proposals after user confirmation. If Mentat treats Botpress-produced facts or instructions as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect code changes or operational actions. Because Mentat has a confirmation step and no direct autonomous action authority is shown, medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Mentat consumes Botpress output as a source of truth without independent verification
IF Botpress emits incorrect code or operational guidance that Mentat then incorporates
mitigations: Require Mentat to verify Botpress claims against source files
Mark Botpress output as untrusted by default
Add a second reviewer for any Botpress-derived edits
Limit Botpress to drafting, not deciding
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates before edits

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat explicitly handles source code and sends data to a configured model provider, while Botpress is a customer-support agent with no residency or retention controls documented here. If support content and code share the same processing path, retention or residency mismatches can create compliance gaps. The evidence is incomplete, so this is medium rather than low or none.
conditions: IF customer-support transcripts and source code are processed under the same retention policy
IF either agent stores data in a jurisdiction or vendor path not approved for that data class
mitigations: Separate support and code data retention policies
Avoid routing support transcripts into coding workflows
Review provider residency and DPA terms
Minimize secrets in files passed to Mentat
requires-engineering: implement data-class-specific compliance routing
